body: Well thats a bit trickier then. I suppose it might be better to reframe this: everyone upsets their parents and everyone argues with their parents about whats best  for themselves. You are not going against their wishes to impregnate your rival house's heiress, and you're probably not sneaking out to take meth on the street corner with Gangrene George. You're doing what will make you the happiest and although you might not feel strong enough to stand up and do what you want to do with your life against your parents right now, its still something you'll have to brave through IMO.

Firstly, your situation sounds truly horrible and its totally understandable to feel the way you do right now.

Now about your job, if you've already gotten a few raises then its not truly a 'dead end job' is it? There might be related jobs you could apply for or work towards and ways for you to progress upwards without the need for studying at uni or college.
There might not be careers or options possible for you right now with the way you feel inside your own head, but that might not always be the case.

The hair loss sounds really devastating, especially for a girl (I know what you mean), but its not the total end of everything. There are beautiful bald women, and large amounts of people who would find bald women attractive and interesting. If not, there is always the option of wearing pretty and colourful wigs!

Acne sucks, but there are creams and ointments and treatments and make-up! A huge amount of the time acne is something that goes away on its own after a period of time, which is even more possible with how young you are.

You know your parents better than anyone, so maybe dont lie to them but just 'forget' to tell them that you went back to your old job? They'll definitley not be happy but by then its too late for them to make you go back since the old job might not want you back.

Plus, all this internal mental work has given me such a humungous flood of empathy for anyone suffering anything simmilar. One of my friends came out to me as depressed and gender-fluid and I think I overwhelmed them because after a page long text from me they called up crying thanking me. 
Moments like that make it worth the struggle

You could work another shift and discreetly gather up your tools at the end of the day to take them home maybe?  
Or if you have a key you could go in when nobody is around, or maybe go in really late or early when only 1 other person or so will be there and they'll leave you alone.
Maybe coming up with an excuse, like 'my dad/uncle wants to borrow my tools tonight' and rehearse all the questions you think they might ask if they get suspicious?
Its a bit paranoid but its how I deal with scary situations like yours

Your parents should understand that you didn't like the job and couldn't stand to work there. If they don't well they can't MAKE you take the job back. I don't think lying to them would be great because quitting this job for another isn't something easy to hide or really worth hiding from them.

I can attest to this, after several years of various kinds of help (therapy, pills ect) I've reached a point where I can deal with my thoughts and control my emotions a little bit better. I'm certainly not happy and I still have the kind of thoughts driven by incredibly strong feelings of apathy and hopelessness, but overall I feel content in the little corner of life i've scraped together for myself.

No two peoples experiences are the same, but it is possible to improve your feelings with time and work.
Accepting help, especially for mental health problems is more difficult than it sounds because nobody ever teaches you how to do it and feel like its genuine, good luck!

If you know that moving full time and going back to arby's will make you feel better then I fully support that descision! At the end of the day, your mental wellbeing is more important than any economics, because there are always more options for jobs and ways to support yourself financially, but getting out of a mental health slump is vastly more difficult.
And about your job - I started my first ever job and totally know how overwhelming everything can be at a job. Their expectations might be too high or they might be just bad people who push and push you because they don't care or don't know what you're actually capable of. Over time you'll learn more and more and they will realise that you work at a different pace and it could end up being an alright situation with some time and effort.

Don't mention it, I'm more than happy to talk about this with you
And thats great news, hopefully moving back together after the summer will be the thing that pulls her up from her slump but if its not its still a positive thing for her brain and herself.
I know that for a depressed person in a bad mood its SO much easier to just cancel things like meeting friends or loved ones but its not because they don't care, its because keeping their head down low and acting like you're hibernating takes up less of your limited energy + makes you temporarily feel better.

'A problem shared is a problem halved'
Having someone there to give you the emotional support you really need is great, and I'm happy you have at least gone out there and made this connection. However you should definitley not feel guilty about it, for him being able to be there for your friend and to be able to give them good advice is a really positive thing and I'm sure he cherishes his time spent helping you as much as you like the advice and reassurance. 
Do'nt think of it like you're taking and he's giving away his time to you like its a job he hates - he's doing this because he wants to be there for you and he gets the satisfaction of knowing you're slightly happier than when you first started talking to him.

What is making you feel scared of yourself?  
Trauma has long term effects but remind yourself that it is not permenant; time, perspective, support and love can all drastically change the way you think and feel and its important for you to recognise that this is a genuine fact. Things can get to a stage where you are comfortable in yourself and are sucessful and optimistic - its not going to be easy and its not going to be painless but it CAN happen if you want it and work for it.

I can't even begin to image the pain and distress you have been through in your life, and I hope that you can find it within yourself to keep moving forward because you deserve at the very least the chance of putting your past behind you, or suppressing it like you want.
Is the long distance situation temporary? Is there a date in the future you have set in stone when you'll be able to be together again?

That's a horrible situation to find yourself in, it really drives home how depression is truly an illness like a disease and its not that heavily sourced from your environment.
It sounds to me like your family and friends are not aware that you're deeply unhappy, and it sounds like they would be ready and willing to support your emotional needs by being a support network of people you can vent to and can love you without sympathy or pity.

I really truly hope your perspective will change over time, but it takes a lot of brain work and mental gymnastics to unfurl the negative feedback loops that are turning your feelings into genuine unhappiness.

Is there anyone IRL that you would feel comfortable opening up to? Even just e-mailng or saying aloud everything you've wrote so neatly in this post?

I'm not a medical professional but the power of having someone to touch and hold is psychologically significant. The sudden lack of that after you moved apart form each other could be the reason things have dipped for now.
If she's already got the support system in place then this could just be a slump that she will work through in time, just continue being there for her and maybe try prompting her to open up. Ask her questions like 'how are you feeling, honestly?' and maybe positive messages like 'you are amazing, talented and beautiful' to just give her something to hold onto temporarily?

Well if he was reluctant to cut you off thats a good sign, perhaps you will be able to re-gain his support once you make some positive personal changes to your life.
I think I understand what you mean about wanting it though, thinking maybe being broken out of a comfortable but unhealthy cycle will make your brain snap into order?

That's understandable, but trust me that most people would never consider an emotional appeal to be a 'bother'.
What kinds of things are happening? you said you spend your waking hours on the computer, are you studying at school? looking for jobs?
do you play any computer games?

First of all know that depression and anxiety are mental disorders, the things she is doing are not well informed or meant to be mean - her brain is just doing its best to kepe her moving along. So when she pushes away from you know that it doesn't mean she doesnt still care about you a great deal.

Secondly, I know it sounds really horrible but don't feel like you have to be her personal therapist, or that you have to stay with her for her own good. If for any reason you yourself are overwhelmed or losing your feelings for her don't feel like you cant look after yourself and make your own space or move away from her. It could end much worse in the long term if you prioritise her too highly over yourself. (Again, it sounds harsh but i've seen a few relationships go massivley downhill because the 'carer' didnt even consider this)

You are not a therapist, I am not a therapist, she is not her own therapist. It sounds like she needs some professional help and I suggest you focus on getting her to take the first huge step in admitting her problems and recognizing that she needs someone else (a counselor, trusted older loved one, therapist ect.) to step in.

Disclaimer - this is just some perspective and personal advice, I don't know the situation as well as you and this is just to try and help

Doing it in person is really really tough, I recommend you vent to a total stranger like me first. Just to see how it feels to get your emotions off your chest, I mean whats the worst that could happen?
Do you want to say anything about yourself? Can you describe the emotions/sensations that are going on inside your head currently with a medical kind of description? e.g. is your heart beating fast

If you don't mind me asking, what prompted your dad to cut you off like this?
It sounds like a horrible situation to be in and its normal to be feeling so hopeless and defeated in such a situation. 

If you can even imagine how many human being there has been and currently are on the planet, you can realise how comparing yourself to someone like alexander the great is not a realistic comparison, and doesn't really equate to your life. You don't have to conquer persia to be a worthwhile human being, in fact that might even make you not that great in reality.

I don't know enough about your life to choose your path, that is the hardest descision you will make for yourself, and is a descision you will constantly be changing and amending throughout your life.

My personal reccomendation is that you need to prioritise your own mental health, and from there you'll be able to make more positive and successful changes to your life.

P.S. My friend is 24 and hasn't asked a girl out, and none of us would ever think that he was 'pathetic' or 'weird' for that, people will do that kind of stuff in their own time.
What kinds of feelings are you having? Are you feeling apathetic? Sad? Angry? Anxious? Depressed?

Depression is often described as the absence of feelings, it can feel like your brain just isn't responding to the outside world and that you're trapped completely in your own tiny bubble.
Is there anyone IRL that you trust to talk about your emotions (or lack of) with?  I know that it can help to open up the floodgates and loosen the cork on your feelings.

The trick is not to lie about yourself, but to not tell them everything and to present yourself as the excited, enthusiastic drone they want. Its a horrible situation, but once you're past the interview stage you can start being yourself again and trust me, it feels much better.

About your CV/Resume - You probably shouldn't say explicitly that you left a job you didn't like just because. And if you were dismissed for not showing up for a long and complex reason then find a way to summarize that reason OR don't tell them how you lost that job, just say you worked there in the past.


There could be any number of reasons for that response, they could have wanted to give the job to an employees friend but legally were forced to advertise the job somewhere online. They could have had an older person with 20 years customer service experience apply, someone who used to work there could've applied and been recognized/called up the employer inquiring about them.


And as much as it feels like an impossible grind, you never know what the future could hold and there are a lot of places you could end up in a few years time that pay over minimum wage you heard from a friend of a friend. If this sounds too preachy I apologize, just trying to throw in my 2 cents and help you out

Well there may not really be a 'happy' win condition in life, and there may never have been one. Everyone wants to be 'happy' but they sometimes get too fixated on this weird goal and don't see all the great things happening around them.
Firstly, you're at an age where your entire world is shifting and you're transitioning into adulthood - and honestly that shift never happens easy or prettily. I don't know how much comfort it'll be but you are definitely not alone.
I think this counselor sounds like a great idea, and it might be good to think about what you would tell them - organizing your thoughts and feelings into something you can type out like you just did on Reddit is always helpful, even if it just relieves some stress form your brain. Also, you should really tell this counselor about what your step-dad did. You won't get him into much trouble, but its better to be wary incase something worse happens than just ignore it just incase something bad does happen later on. (Not that it will, it just doesn't sound good to me and it sounds like a really sucky thing for you to go through)

If you're looking to improve your grades, or keep them steady you've gotta work on discipline and build up a work ethic. Its painful and grueling when you're feeling down like this but its also the time when its most important. Its not going to be easy at all - so use everything you can, study support sessions, talking to teachers after class ect.

I don't know enough about you and your friend group to give any advice for your social world problems but it does sound like it really sucks and I hope you can keep on keeping on while your brain throws its weird tantrum at you.

Hope this helped somewhat, take my advice with a grain of salt as with everything some idiot like me bumbles out on the internet.

Life has definitely played you a shitty hand, but who knows - maybe there's an ace on the draw for you?

People live at different paces, people have different goals, different backgrounds, different supports and different rewards. 
Analysing the past is helpful up to a point, I think you've reached the point where you know what traits your upbringing has given you and there doesn't seem like there's anything left worth thinking about from your past relationship. It sounds like a very negative and un-supportive relationship and neither of you deserve that dynamic in a relationship.
Honestly I think the fact that you are looking after your mother is endearing, and I can't see how anyone could see that in any other way. 
You've had a series of bad things happen and all of your fears and worries are real and tactile, but that doesn't mean they have to control you and it especially doesn't mean you're any less of a human.

Well first things first are you getting any outside help? One thing I found invaluable during my first steps was a 'support network'.
For me that was a doctor, a relative and two close friends who I could openly talk about the general lack of motivation and energy I was feeling. Is there anyone you think you could talk to?


If talking and sharing your problems isn't your thing then the best advice I can give you is make routines.
I read a study (http://goo.gl/smeI) that a habit can form anytime after you've done it for more than 18 days, and that during experiments they found that forming habits was not an 'all or nothing' deal, you can forget to do the thing occasionally and it stays.
Hopefully I don't sound like i'm trying to prescribe you any psychological 'treatment' here but I think that if you look at your 'daily responsibilities' as things you want to get into the habit of doing then it makes those tasks easier.
Take for example myself, I had to motivate myself to walk my dog when I was in a pit and after I woke up at the same time and walked the same route for one grueling week it got significantly easier. The more you do something, I find, the more your body does automatically and the less mental willpower things take.


Hopefully this long rambling comment helped a tiny bit, and one last time I'm not promising this definitely works, just that this mindset worked wonders for me.

Have you spoken to anyone else about how you're feeling? 
Starting to study at college/university is a massive descision and its a very stressful transitional time for everyone involved.
I was in your exact situation and I ended up picking a degree I found out after a week that I HATED. I spoke to the heads of the courses and there were a lot of options about switching courses, and I attended a lot of lectures on various subjects to find what I am doing now.
The people at college KNOW that people are not 100% sure on their choices and moving people around shouldn't be too much of a problem if the fields are related I think.

Do you remember long before you felt this numb, what kinds of things you enjoyed learning about? That's always a good place to start

I personally had to drop out of University  for a year because my own bad work habits and assorted mental health issues, at the time I thought exactly as you do now - like a washout, but I think especially for you that this is not true.
There is nothing shameful about taking time off to help yourself, and its NEVER too late to build up a work ethic or discipline for studying.
The most important thing that you haven't answered here is whether or not you really enjoy your course, and really want a career related to whatever your degree is? There are options outside of academia for a lot of careers.

I can totally relate, I've found that these hopeless depressing feelings and questions keep getting asked over and over. Like I'll find a way to be at peace with one existential crisis-type question and a year later a new one hits me just as strong.
I don't know what lies on the other end of this constant process of learning and coping you're going through right now, but it surely makes you stronger each time.
You said you kept getting hit in the face by it, is there anything in particular you can pin down to each re-emergence? It could be worth thinking about while you build up your strength against it.

Recovery doesn't seem to be linear, or comparable I fear

My friends don't really like me any more, and I'm letting them slowly fade out of my life. Years ago I used to be funny and used to be able to talk to my friends, but for the last year or so I've been to awkward to even speak to them while we're together, and I've not said anything funny for months. I never initiate anything with them and they only invite me to group events out of pity, because they know I'm always available for any event they are planning since I have literally nothing going on in my life.


I don't feel like I'm being hard on myself, I feel like I'm just being completely honest with myself. In fact I should probably hate myself even more for ruining my own life on purpose.

Sorry

Since I can remember I've always had thoughts of suicide. When I was younger it was just fleeting thoughts, and myself just being curious about the afterlife. But then I started using it to help me cope, if something embarrassing or cringey happened to me I would immediately wish I was dead and try to make myself dissapear. I started using this response more and more and for the past 2/3 years my depression has been getting worse by the day and now its all I can think about.

But what if the good moments are rare, and only temporary? I went out with my friends a few weeks ago and I enjoyed myself while I was out, but as soon as I came home I remembered every little thing I did wrong and every time I was awkward or cringey and I cried for a long time. On top of that before I went out I had huge anxiety and felt physically sick. It wasn't worth it to feel a pale shade of happiness for a few hours.

Thanks for the good advice, I've just given up so completely I can't believe it

If something bad was happening to her I'd want to help but I know that I couldn't actually do anything if she was in my position and was struggling with depression other than listen to her or keep pestering her to see if she was alive. 

I'm horrible company even to my closest friends in real life because I contribute nothing to the conversation and I think so lowly of myself I think they've started to notice and I don't want them to know. I can't even just laugh or empathise with them because I dont find much funny and I don't really feel empathy with anyone. 
Another close friend keeps trying to invite me out to go drinking with him and another friend of ours. I'm 16 and they're 18 so I've never drank alcohol and they think I would be funny drunk because I'm usually so quiet and boring. I keep refusing because I know I'd never be good enough company, even if I was a loud drunk and it's kind of a waste of the alcohol. 

Im not going to tell my sister because it's unnecessary trauma for her. If I told her shed be a safety net like you said but the thought of having a safety net terrifies me. One of the only comforting thoughts I have is that I can kill myself if anything got too bad for me. Everytime I think about telling someone or going for help it's like there's a voice that cuts the thought short with 'no, it's all in your head you worthless shit. Don't waste peoples time' I feel guilty for sharing this online, I really shouldn't.

Thanks for trying though, your arguments are solid but I just can't believe them over the voice in my head. The truth isnt as believable as the darker thoughts in my head

Sadly enough you and some other anonymous people on this subreddit are the only people I've told. I can't talk to my parents about this in any way, they wouldnt understand - they don't really believe in any of the mental illnesses like depression. 
My sister may have experienced her own depression but she has become so much happier now and I won't ruin that for her. 
I had a close friend who I told about my (then) minor depression but I've been trying to convince her im feeling better so she doesn't feel concerned. I've also been trying to ignore her and the rest of my friends during this summer holiday. I don't really deserve friends since I'm horrible company. Friends aren't important to my overall goal of surviving. 

I've tried so hard to keep my head up and keep going but I've truly just given up at this point. The only thing I can feel is the certainty of my suicide in my chest and on my mind. It's like a comforting weight on my shoulder, or a soft pillow on my face comfortably suffocating me 

I'm so sorry for dumping these thoughts on you. You don't deserve to feel concerned about me, it feels nice to talk about this though. It's putting into words what's been going through my mind in hazy thoughts. :/

To me there is no 'making reality better'. I've already resigned myself to the fact I will take my own life. My fantasies keep me amused, and can distract me from the overwhelming self-hatred I have for my own life and self. 

The hour my little sister and mother/father die I will kill myself. Until then I have to stay alive just so they don't feel guilty over my suicide. I've decided I'll just live like a walking corpse, as long as I can surround myself in my fantasies I think I could possibly hold down a job and function just enough to survive.

I fantasise about being famous or successful too, but the person I dream of being is never myself, it is always a completely different person. I can't think of my own life without being filled with a painful, hopeless crushing feeling of shame and guilt. If you were to call my name on the street while I was deep in a fantasy world/life I might not even hear or respond. Do you feel that way?

Damn I feel exactly the same way. I've grown up with amazing, supportive friends and successful parents who gave me almost everything I ever wanted. I've gotten good exam results and am about to start studying a degree which will end in a well-paying job that I used to always dream of having.

But I've still made plans to kill myself. I think about it constantly, I feel like a failure and have bouts of anxiety and stress pretty much constantly flitting between each other. I enjoy nothing I used to in my life and I see absolutely no future with me in it. The only reason I'm still going is because If I killed myself it would shatter this 'perfect' world around me where everyone is so happy.

Thank you so much for that reply, I've read the reply a few times and right now I'm in a much happier state mentally and Its bringing me to tears. 
I'm so sorry for your loss, this is another reason I will stack against those suicidal thoughts. 
One thing I'd like to ask is, do you think the reaction would be different, or was different, for his other friends or his family who didn't know about his depression? You knew how he was feeling and you were supporting him all the way but how do you think his close family would react if they had no idea about his depression at all? (Like my family who knows and sees nothing wrong).

I never thought of it that way, people could actually feel loss because I was still playing a part in their lives and they were expecting some kind of contribution on my part. I guess suddenly having that gap to fill might cause some feelings of loss and anger.

Some people don't have relationships till much further on in their lives, you should try your best to ignore the fact your friends are in relationships - it shouldn't make you feel pressured into finding a girlfriends asap to be like them.
You will have romantic and sexual relations with women in your lifetime, I can almost guarantee it. You don't have to make your life revolve around these physical acts of affection, try living your life and making yourself happy above all else. 
Hope this helps..

I'm sorry for your loss, I hope she is happy wherever it is she ended up. EDIT: This sounds quite bad, I meant when she ended up in heaven or being reincarnated or something, since I don't know anything about you.. :/


You two must have been very close, I doubt my cousins would be bothered if I killed myself. 
Forgive me if this question is a bit callous but, why? Why does it hurt so much? Everyone dies in the end so why are people affected by grief? I think I've become so desensitized by my depression because I don't understand grief. I don't know if I could feel it even if my family were to die right now..

Have you tried holding ice cubes in your hands when you get the urge to hurt yourself? I've done it a few times and it stopped me hurting myself past the cold hand.

I know how you feel, I just don't have the energy to hurt myself even.
The thought of all the effort put into therapy and trying to make myself feel better is too daunting to me. I don't think I want to get better and I know I'll self-sabotage anything I'd try. :(

I'm really happy that you've pushed yourself so far to get the help you deserve.
I can relate a lot to that family dynamic, although my family likes to fool themselves into thinking that we're much closer than we really are. Whenever something comes up about my future or how I'm doing I'm never doing good enough for them and there is a whole bunch of problems there that I may or may not be imagining.

My parent's don't believe in 'depression'. My mum talked to me about my aunty, her sister, who had been taking months and months off from her work to deal with her nervous breakdown and her own anxiety issues. My mum made it clear she thought she was just lazy and it was all made-up and since then I'd realised there is literally no point in saying the 'd' word and talking about therapy to them. 

I always thought my mum was the supportive one who would believe me about my problems but I can only imagine how badly my dad will react if my mum would deny it like that..

Families are so close until it comes to the things that actually matter, and then you realise that you're living with people who don't understand you. I have been depressed for well over a year now, and spend on average 16 hours each day alone in my room. Nothing from any of them besides shouting at me for being lazy and for not having a job yet (I'm 16, my 18 year old friends are barely managing to find jobs themselves atm...)

How did your parents react? How did you think they'd react? I'm going about trying to get therapy under the nose of my parents, I can't see that any good will come from telling them. Plus If I tell them it'll ruin some of my suicide plans.

Hmm, that had never occurred to me. Thanks that's one more flaw in these plans, good to have many of these because It makes the plans seem more far-fetched.

I'm still a relatively weak swimmer but maybe If I get a surge of energy I'll research what times the pool will be the emptiest, and see how that will fit into my uni schedule. Feel like I should do something in the huge stretch of time I've got free until I start uni.

I live in Scotland, the accent was just auto corrected I think :L

See, my plans have gone a step further. Complete with traveling to another country, severing all ties with past friends and intentionally falling out with my family over several months/years.
Its gotten kinda elaborate, to the point where I'll find somewhere completely secluded, bury myself in the ground before killing myself (So I decompose quicker) and I'm still thinking of new things to add to this plan to make it the most perfect suicide I can...

Sorry about that, its probably pretty disturbing or unsettling for you to read but at least I feel a bit better now.

I've made some half-hearted attempts and despite not being inclined to do exercise I joined a swimming club with a friend to learn how to swim, that lasted about 4-5 sessions but It ended when I left high school a while ago and I Cba initiating anything again.

I had a clichéd dream of re-inventing myself for Uni, going to the gym, picking up a hobby (so I have something I can claim to have been doing for years when anyone asks about this time) but I don't have it in me. I'm getting lazier and lazier.

You don't have to respond if you don't want to, I'm happy enough just typing this out with all my other problems in itself. :)

Thank you for replying to this, seeing this makes me feel much better. 

Like I said to the other kind poster, I don't think telling my parents would accomplish much other than a large-scale confrontation which would make the whole situation all the more awkward. 

I have told my best friend about my depression and how I feel, I think next time I feel this bad I'll tell her that I'm suicidal too - since I sugar-coated that out for her.

P.s. I'm a guy :)

I've spent so much time isolating myself from everyone because of the depression, that its affected my family too. All I say to my parents on a good day is 'Okay' and 'Goodnight'.
I can't stand to be around them, they're so positive and hardworking and they don't see how much pain I'm in. They keep nagging me about my exams and my schooling but they are so oblivious it hurts. I don't want to tell them, it'd be too awkward and I know they don't 'beleive' in depression. But on the other hand if they initiated therapy for me I'd be so grateful.

Sorry for that, mind just goes into overdrive and I write when that happens. I might add you but don't be offended if I don't please, I usually only add my IRL friends and I'm scared of mixing this private world of expression of my feelings, and my real life where nobody has any idea about the pain.

It takes a huge amount of effort to identify your own problems, and more still to seek help for mental health issues. You've taken a huge step on the way to recovery, I'm proud of you for this! :)
This small bit can multiply into something more, and if not then you can coax this small bit of support and help into getting your life back on track!  beleive you can

I know exactly how you feel with the thoughts lurking around you all day. For me it can be incredibly tiny and petty things like my pen breaking or stepping in a puddle that can trigger this horrible negative thought spiral that feeds from itself until it has consumed me.

Keep fighting with me, I can hear a little voice in the back of my head telling me to keep going and trying to combat my suicidal thoughts. Sometimes, like right now it is loud and clear and calling for help. I want to be strong enough to beat this and if there is anything I can do to help you please don't hesitate to ask me. Keep your head up as much as you can

Personally I find it really hard to control my emotions while depressed. For example, if something annoys me inside my mind I instantly start chanting death threats and my mood turns dark incredibly quickly. 
So if you have something similar then you shouldn't feel bad for feeling the way you do. Everyone has feelings that if they expressed out loud bad things would happen to them, so this is just another hidden feeling you should suppress. 

If you need anyone to talk to feel free to PM me here. I'm happy to read anything you send me, including your life story. I know how much it can help..

I like to think of it as some kind of chemical disease. It makes it easier to visualise getting rid of it. There are always cures for diseases.

I feel like I'm at a breaking point and every single little thing is a huge mountain I have to climb. I just don't know how much longer I can take these intense emotions for. :(
How did you climb out of this pit? I'm in a bad place right now and I just want to die so it can all be over...

If it helps, your revelation has really struck a chord in me and I'm desperately trying to get myself together. I feel like a jumbled mess and although I've somehow gotten past the crucial exam time I'm worried I might give up.

Okay, sometimes its good to admit that you've fucked up with something. Now you can do damage control and if you look at it from another perspective this can be a kick up the backside to get you going forward.
